title: A message is written only inside the caller's transaction
statement: A message MUST be written only inside the caller's transaction, after its payload is checked, and a notice MUST follow the commit and never precede it.

title: One worker holds one message under a lease
statement: A message MUST be claimed by at most one worker at a time under a lease, only the current lease MUST be able to finish it, and a late result MUST NOT count as a success.

title: Delivery is in order per key
statement: Messages MUST be delivered in order within one key, a retry MUST block only its own key and MUST keep the message identity, and an unknown destination MUST stay queued.

title: A database failure is never a delivery
statement: A database failure MUST NOT be counted as a delivery, a lost claim result MUST keep the lease, a failed claim MUST return nothing, and a process crash MUST leave every rule intact.

title: The worker and its subscriptions are bounded
statement: Worker concurrency and subscriptions MUST be bounded by checked limits, a lost session MUST stop every subscription, and shutdown MUST finish a completed delivery and return a cancellation as such.

title: The queue keeps no error text, and the blocked view lists each stuck key once
statement: The queue MUST store no error text or payload copy, and the blocked view MUST list each stuck key once.

title: The delay from commit to delivery is measured per destination
statement: The worker MUST record, for each message that reaches done, the time from its enqueue in the caller's transaction to done as the histogram outbox.delivery.delay in seconds labelled by destination only, and MUST report the age of the oldest message of each destination that is not done as the gauge outbox.oldest.age, so the time a committed change takes to reach its destination is known and can be alerted on.

title: A message moves only through the dispatch states
statement: A message MUST be in exactly one of the states pending, dispatching, outcome unknown, reconciling, done, parked and discarded, and MUST move only by these transitions: pending to dispatching by a claim; dispatching to done, to pending, also when the handler returns a conflict (ST-SUP-RP01-LC18), to outcome unknown or to parked; outcome unknown to dispatching, to reconciling or to parked; reconciling to done, to pending, to parked or to reconciling again; and parked to done, to pending or to discarded by a person; any other transition MUST be refused and MUST leave the message as it was.

title: An outcome is unknown when the request may have reached the destination
statement: An error that the handler marks as a conflict MUST end in pending as ST-SUP-RP01-LC18 states, also when the attempt's deadline has passed. Otherwise, an attempt MUST end in outcome unknown when its deadline passes, when the connection is lost after the request was sent, when the handler returns an error that it does not mark as not sent, as refused by the destination or as a conflict, or when its lease expires while it is dispatching; only a success MUST end in done, an error marked as not sent or as a transient refusal MUST end in pending, an error marked as a conflict MUST end in pending as ST-SUP-RP01-LC18 states, and an error marked as a permanent refusal MUST end in parked.

title: An unknown outcome is sent again only to an idempotent destination, with the same key
statement: From outcome unknown, a message MUST be dispatched again only when its destination is registered as idempotent, and every attempt MUST send the same outgoing idempotency key, which the message stores at enqueue as the key that Derive gives (ST-SUP-RP07-LC06), or as its message identity when no inbound key exists; a message for a destination that is not registered as idempotent MUST NOT be dispatched again from outcome unknown.

title: Reconciling asks the destination's status lookup
statement: From outcome unknown, a message for a destination that is not idempotent and registers a status lookup MUST move to reconciling, and the worker MUST call the lookup with the message identity and its outgoing key only after the attempt's deadline plus the destination's settle time has passed; a lookup that answers acted MUST move the message to done, one that answers not acted MUST move it to pending, and an answer of unknown or an error MUST keep it in reconciling with a backoff until the lookup bound, a worker setting whose default is 10 lookups, moves it to parked.

title: A message with no safe next step is parked with an alert
statement: A message MUST move to parked when its outcome is unknown and its destination is neither idempotent nor has a status lookup, when its lookups are exhausted, when its handler marks a permanent refusal, or when its attempts are exhausted; parking MUST record the state the message left, MUST raise one alert event and metric that name the destination and that state, MUST hold back the later messages of its key and MUST NOT hold back another key.

title: A person resolves a parked message
statement: Resolve MUST accept only a parked message, with an allow for the resolve permission (ST-SUP-RP01-LC17), the subject of the person who resolves it and the outcome they chose: acted, not acted, or discarded; for a destination registered as idempotent it MUST accept only not acted, or discarded when the destination must land, because sending it again is safe and acted would lose what the delivery records; acted MUST move the message to done, not acted to pending with the same identity and outgoing key, and discarded to discarded, which releases its key; discarded MUST be refused for a destination that need not land; the resolution MUST write its audit row in the same transaction as the state change; and a resolution without an allow, or of a message in any other state, MUST be refused and change nothing.

title: A destination is registered with its idempotency and its status lookup
statement: A destination MUST be registered on the worker with its name, its handler, whether it is idempotent, whether its messages must land, and an optional status lookup with its settle time; a destination that does not say it is idempotent or must land MUST count as neither; a status lookup without a positive settle time MUST be refused; and a destination that is neither idempotent nor has a status lookup MUST be accepted, and its unknown outcomes MUST be parked.

title: An unknown outcome is claimed under a lease and holds back its key
statement: A claim MUST move a dispatching message whose lease has expired to outcome unknown in the same statement, before it claims anything for that key; a message in outcome unknown or reconciling MUST be claimed under a lease as a pending one is, when its backoff time has come, by the worker that then takes its next step; and a message in dispatching, outcome unknown or reconciling MUST hold back the later messages of its key, so a refund never overtakes a charge whose outcome is unknown.

title: Purge removes only parked messages that may go
statement: Listing dead letters MUST return only parked messages, and purge MUST remove only parked messages, in bounded batches, and MUST NOT remove one that left outcome unknown or reconciling, or one of a destination registered as must land, until a person resolves it; purge MUST NOT remove a discarded message.

title: Resolve decides the resolve permission itself
statement: Resolve MUST itself ask the decision port the worker is built with whether the person's subject has the permission resolve on the resource outbox_destination:<destination name>, at the consistency floor of ST-SUP-RP06-LC09, and MUST refuse a deny or a port error; a worker built without a decision port MUST refuse every resolution; and Resolve MUST NOT take a decision from its caller.

title: A consumer conflict is dispatched again with backoff and is not an attempt
statement: When a handler returns an error marked as a conflict, such as RunConsumer does (ST-SUP-RP10-LC26), the dispatch MUST move the message from dispatching to pending (ST-SUP-RP01-LC08), MUST NOT count an attempt, MUST count one conflict in a counter of the message, MUST make the message due again after a wait that starts at 100 ms, doubles at each conflict in a row up to 30 s and has random jitter, and MUST hold back the later messages of its key while it waits, as for a retry. A dispatch that does not end in a conflict MUST set the counter to zero. After 20 conflicts in a row, the dispatch MUST count each further conflict as a failed attempt, so a message that does not stop conflicting still ends as the attempts limit states (ST-SUP-RP01-LC12).

title: Every item reaches its action unchanged, one key at a time
statement: A queued item MUST reach its action with its content unchanged and never merged with another, equal keys MUST run serially while other keys continue, and a change that arrives during a key's action MUST request a later pass.

title: The queue is bounded with backpressure
statement: Worker count, key capacity and reconnect delay MUST be refused outside their bounds, and each producer MUST hold at most one key waiting for admission.

title: Retries are off by default, bounded, and retry only the action
statement: The zero retry policy MUST make one attempt, a policy MUST be refused beyond four attempts or outside one millisecond to one second of delay, each attempt MUST get a fresh budget, cancellation MUST stop a delay, and a scan, window, checkpoint or denied error MUST NOT be retried.

title: A reconnect keeps the schedule
statement: Across watch sessions the queue MUST keep its keys, their order, due times, capacity and a failed scan's capped backoff, and an interrupted action MUST run again.

title: Scans resume after the last success with opaque cursors
statement: A scan MUST resume from the cursor of the last item whose action succeeded, MUST treat cursors as opaque and refuse an oversized or non-UTF-8 one before any read, and MUST return incomplete progress without error at its page budget.

title: A stream is bounded and closed
statement: A stream MUST have separate open and receive limits, MUST stop with the scan contract error past its item limit, MUST be cancelled and joined when the scan returns, and a value the receive function returns after its receive timeout MUST NOT reach the emitter.

title: Each operation is its own trace with a fixed outcome, and telemetry holds no private value
statement: Each reconciliation, scan and sweep MUST start its own trace root, MUST end with exactly one of success, failure, timeout or cancelled, and no metric, snapshot or exposition MUST carry a key, payload, error text or resource ID.

title: Overlapping controllers share one private provider set, and a failed callback emits one event
statement: Overlapping controllers in one process MUST share one private telemetry provider set that the first starts and the last closes, the monitor MUST bind loopback only, and a callback failure MUST emit exactly one service.failed event with no formatted cause.

title: A retry never outruns its budget
statement: A retry delay MUST be refused when it exceeds the action timeout; a failed attempt MUST be cancelled and its callback joined before the delay starts; no further attempt MUST start when the remaining work budget cannot cover the delay and a full action; a terminal peer failure MUST cancel the pending retries of a parallel cycle; and a later success MUST NOT clear a failure already stored in the cycle checkpoint.

title: Backoff follows its cause
statement: A failed connection attempt MUST NOT delay keys already queued, an interrupted action MUST take the next capped delay rather than a reset one, a successful scan MUST clear the scan backoff, and a queued action MUST be able to run while the next scan waits for its due time.

title: Admission never blocks a producer
statement: The scan cursor MUST advance only after the item is admitted, the page request context MUST end before the scan waits for admission, admission MUST stop on cancellation, and adding a key MUST NOT block the caller.

title: One collector per controller, fixed in size
statement: A collector that another running controller holds MUST be refused; the collector MUST expose a fixed instrument set, queue capacity, queued, active, retrying, waiting and ready, completed actions by outcome, retries, completed scans, reconnects and one fixed duration histogram, with no configurable label and a size that does not grow with the resource count; counters MUST survive a reconnect and gauges MUST reset when the queue stops; and a cancelled action MUST schedule no retry in a stopped queue while an interrupted scan MUST NOT count as completed.

title: The monitor serves metrics on loopback only, within fixed limits
statement: The monitor MUST serve the metrics, and nothing else, in Prometheus text format with no-store and nosniff, answer not found to any other path and method not allowed to any other method, register on no default mux, bind loopback only, and run with header, read, write and idle limits and the http.Server MaxHeaderBytes setting of 4096, which Go enforces with its own margin of 4096 bytes; an empty address MUST give a nil collector and no server; a listener failure MUST stop the controller from starting; and when either part exits the monitor MUST close the listener, cancel the shared context and join both.

title: Startup shares one telemetry runtime
statement: The monitor MUST start the telemetry runtime before the application callback and hold it for the callback's whole life, so that setup, nested controllers and deferred cleanup share one runtime and one instance identity; it MUST wait for an ongoing bounded provider close; each queue MUST register once, unregister when its run ends, and be refused beyond sixty-four; cancellation MUST emit no failure event; the callback's value and error identity MUST return unchanged; and a probe command MUST start no telemetry.

title: Each operation logs once, at a severity its outcome sets
statement: Each reconcile, scan and watch MUST emit one completion log and one duration sample that carry the operation, the outcome, the retry flag and the span's trace and span IDs, valid also when unsampled; a watch span MUST cover one session and end before reconnect; the log MUST be INFO for success and cancellation, WARN for a failure that retries and ERROR for one that does not; watch start, reconnect and cleanup-summary failure MUST be fixed events; and the instruments MUST be the fixed stego.controller.* set with no configurable label.

title: A sweep validates first and classifies each failure
statement: A sweep MUST validate every definition before it starts telemetry and MUST start no provider when its context is already cancelled; it MUST register no keyed queue; a pass deadline MUST count as a retry only while the run is active and the error is not terminal; a page callback that returns no error after its deadline MUST be recorded as a timeout and MUST NOT become a source error for the terminal policy; and the sweep MUST join its workers before the next page and before close.

title: Scan progress is exact
statement: On a source or emitter error a resumed scan MUST return the progress of the completed prefix together with the error; it MUST refuse a page above its size bound and bound each page read by the operation timeout; a scan from the beginning MUST return the scan contract error, not partial progress, when its page budget cannot cover the source; and a scan MUST start no background work.

title: Cleanup sampling is its own bounded worker
statement: With metrics enabled the runtime MUST read the cleanup summary on its own worker, under the action timeout and at the resync interval, join it on shutdown, and never read it when metrics are disabled; a failed read MUST keep the last values but mark them unavailable, shutdown MUST mark them unavailable, a malformed sample or a terminal access error MUST stop the controller, any other failure MUST be reported and sampled again, and a failed sample MUST keep its own counter and never count as a work retry.

title: An operation root keeps its context and bounds its span
statement: An operation root MUST keep the supplied context's cancellation, deadline and runtime ownership and change trace ancestry only; a database span MUST be a child of the current operation; sampling MUST apply to each operation root; a controller span or log MUST carry no resource key, provider response, credential or private error text; and attribute and link counts per span MUST stay within the default limits.

title: Without a collector, no provider
statement: When no collector endpoint is set the runtime MUST start no provider and open no connection, and the service MUST serve as if telemetry were absent, except the built-in console events of ST-SUP-RP12-LC22.

title: Export is bounded, verified and never retried
statement: Export MUST go over one verified HTTPS gRPC connection owned by private providers with no global, each export MUST finish inside its deadline, send at most one MiB and never be retried, and startup MUST NOT wait for the collector.

title: Queues drop rather than block, and failures are counted safely
statement: The trace and log queues MUST be bounded and drop rather than block the request, and each failed export batch MUST be counted per signal and answered with a fixed safe error.

title: One span per request or call, named by the pattern, never the URL
statement: The runtime MUST start one server span per HTTP request and one RPC span covering the whole call, named by the method and the registered route or protobuf method when bounded and _OTHER otherwise, and never by the URL.

title: A failure marks the span without a message
statement: A status of 500 or more, a panic or a failing RPC status MUST mark the span with a fixed error type and MUST NOT attach a message, a cause or a value.

title: Every call is measured and logged once, sampled or not, with no private data
statement: Request duration metrics and one completion log per call MUST exist whether or not the span is sampled, MUST be correlated with the span when it is, and MUST hold no raw path, resource ID, body, credential or user detail.

title: The server span starts before authentication and ends with the transport status
statement: The HTTP and RPC server span MUST start before authentication and capacity admission and end only after the final status is known, MUST NOT change authentication, capacity reservation, stream identity expiry, I/O deadlines or shutdown of the observed call, and the public health and discovery routes MUST stay outside the request span, metric and log wrappers.

title: A valid parent continues the trace, and the remote flag never decides sampling
statement: A single valid traceparent MUST continue its trace ID and parent ID, and the remote sampled flag MUST NOT change the local ratio decision at any ratio.

title: Settings have fixed defaults and a fixed shape
statement: With a collector endpoint and no exporter setting, traces, metrics and request logs MUST be enabled; the sampling ratio MUST default to 0.1, the metric export interval to ten seconds and the service name to the declared service name; the protocol setting MUST be absent or grpc; and the certificate setting MUST be read only as a bounded regular PEM file, with the system roots when it is absent.

title: Export limits are fixed numbers
statement: The trace queue MUST hold at most 256 spans, exported in batches of at most 32; each export MUST end within two seconds with a 64 KiB response limit; and shutdown MUST give the provider at most three seconds.

title: Request metrics have fixed names, units and labels
statement: The runtime MUST emit http.server.request.duration and rpc.server.call.duration as histograms in seconds with fixed boundaries through 1,800 seconds and cumulative temporality, labelled by method, registered route or RPC method, status and a fixed error class; MUST emit http.server.active_requests and rpc.server.active_requests as label-free up-down counters; and MUST NOT use a trace or span ID as a metric label.

title: A completion log has a fixed name and a severity its outcome sets
statement: The completion log MUST be named http.server.request.completed or rpc.server.call.completed, MUST carry the span's fields, the duration and the trace and span IDs, and MUST be INFO for a normal completion, WARN for a denied or failed client request and ERROR for a server failure.

title: The RPC span records a fixed attribute set
statement: The RPC server span MUST record exactly rpc.system.name, rpc.method and rpc.response.status_code with one of the seventeen gRPC status names; only UNKNOWN, DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, UNIMPLEMENTED, INTERNAL, UNAVAILABLE and DATA_LOSS MUST mark it failed, with error.type equal to that status name; and no server span MUST carry a resource ID, a user identity, a peer address or error text.

title: The route pattern survives a copied request and zero sampling
statement: The span, metric and log MUST carry the registered route pattern also when authentication copies the request and when the sampling ratio is zero, and metrics and logs MUST NOT take their fields from recorded span attributes.

title: A Tenant is never zero and comes only from its four sources
statement: A Tenant MUST be built only through the one constructor and from one of four sources: a verified identity claim, by the authentication component; an entry of the tenant list, by the iterator for a worker tick or a controller (ST-SUP-RP04-LC07); or the tenant column of a claimed outbox row, by the outbox worker, which the staging transaction wrote from its own tenant (ST-SUP-RP10-LC16); or the tenant that a Provision or Retire request names, only after its permission is decided (ST-SUP-RC27-OC09). Every function that takes a Tenant MUST refuse the zero value before any statement is sent, and a client-supplied header or body field and a message payload MUST NOT be accepted as a source, other than the tenant that a decided Provision or Retire request names.

title: The context carries one tenant or fails
statement: Reading the tenant from the request context MUST return the tenant the authentication component set there, and MUST return an error and never a zero tenant when none is set, so no code path reachable from a request runs without a tenant.

title: Every transaction starts with a transaction-local tenant setting
statement: The transaction helper MUST run SELECT set_config('app.tenant', $1, true) as the first statement of every transaction it opens, before the caller's first statement, and MUST NOT run a session-scoped SET or set_config with is_local false.

title: The pooler guard refuses a session setting
statement: The guard MUST refuse at startup a connection option, a startup parameter or a statement that sets a session-scoped value, and MUST verify on the first connection that current_setting('app.tenant', true) is empty outside a transaction, so a pooled connection never carries one tenant to the next client.

title: A multi-tenant worker opens one transaction per tenant
statement: Each MUST iterate the tenants it is given and open one transaction per tenant with that tenant set, MUST NOT share a transaction between two tenants, and MUST continue with the next tenant after one tenant's function fails and report every failure at the end.

title: The owner connector serves only the migration job
statement: The owner-role connector MUST open only when the process runs the migration job and MUST refuse to open in the api, worker or controller mode, and the runtime connector MUST verify at startup that its role owns no table and holds no BYPASSRLS and fail startup otherwise.

title: The tenant list is the tenants table that provisioning writes
statement: The iterator MUST read the tenants that it visits from the table stego_tenants of the service's database, in tenant ID order, as the runtime role, and MUST skip each tenant that has a retire time; only Provision and Retire of the tenant runtime, which the generated service serves as its own commands (ST-SUP-RC27-OC09), MUST write that table, Retire MUST set the retire time and delete no row, and each MUST run the provisioning hooks that the generated code registers in the same transaction as its write, with that tenant set, so a hook's writes commit with the tenant or not at all.

title: An audit event has a fixed shape, and its request fields are untrusted
statement: Event MUST carry exactly id (UUID v7), occurred_at, recorded_at, tenant_id, actor_id, actor_kind (user, service, system or impersonated_by), actor_ip, user_agent, action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome (ok, denied or failed), error_code, request_id, trace_id, span_id, idempotency_key, before, after, patch, service, service_version, declaration_version, prev_hash and hash; actor_ip and user_agent MUST be marked untrusted and MUST NOT decide anything.

title: The audit row commits with the change, or alone with its outcome
statement: Recording an audit entry MUST insert the row through the caller's transaction and MUST NOT commit on its own, recording an outcome MUST write the row of a denied or failed mutation in its own short transaction with the outcome and error_code, and a read of an entity that holds a pii field MUST be recorded in its own short transaction with the action read, so the read row stays when the caller's transaction rolls back.

title: Redaction before storage: pii is redacted, secret is never stored
statement: The encoder MUST replace every field declared pii in before, after and patch, at any depth of a nested value, with the fixed redaction marker before hashing and storing, also when the service's Audit setting declares audit.pii keep (ST-DECL-EN10), which keeps the field in the source record only, and MUST drop every field declared secret, at any depth, before it encodes a value, so it reaches neither the row, the hash, the sink nor an error message.

title: The hash is SHA-256 over the canonical redacted record and prev_hash, in one chain per tenant
statement: The canonical encoding MUST be deterministic, with sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace and one form for numbers and times; hash MUST be SHA-256 over the canonical redacted record followed by prev_hash; each tenant of each service MUST have its own chain (ST-STD-TXN-R01), in which each row has a seq one higher than the row before it; prev_hash MUST be the hash of the previous row of the same chain, and the first row's prev_hash MUST be 32 zero bytes.

title: The patch is RFC 6902 over the redacted states
statement: Diff MUST produce an RFC 6902 patch from the redacted before to the redacted after, applying that patch to before MUST yield after exactly, and a metadata-level event MUST carry neither before, after nor patch.

title: The verifier walks one tenant's chain from its checkpoint and checks it against every anchor
statement: Verify MUST walk one tenant's chain in seq order in a transaction of that tenant (ST-SUP-RP04-LC03), from the row after the chain's latest retention checkpoint (ST-SUP-RP05-LC11) with the checkpoint's hash as the first prev_hash, or from the first row with 32 zero bytes when the chain has no checkpoint. It MUST recompute every hash and report the first row whose prev_hash or hash differs, and MUST report a first row whose seq is not one higher than the checkpoint's seq. For each periodic anchor that the sink holds for the chain, it MUST compare the hash of the row whose seq equals the anchor's count with the anchor's head, MUST report truncation when the highest seq is lower than the latest anchor's count, and MUST report as forged an anchor whose count is lower than an earlier anchor's count or whose head is not on the chain. It MUST check each row as it reads it and keep only the previous hash and the anchors, so its memory does not grow with the chain.

title: Every audit row is enqueued for the sink, keyed by its id
statement: Record MUST enqueue the same event in the outbox for the audit sink in the same transaction, with the message key equal to the event id, and the destination MUST deliver it through the Sink port and treat a duplicate id as success, so the sink is idempotent.

title: The sink is a port with no way back
statement: The Sink port MUST expose only Append(events) and Anchor(anchor), where an anchor holds the tenant, the kind periodic or retention, the head hash and the count; the runtime MUST NOT expose an update, a delete or a read on it, and the service MUST reach the sink only through the outbox destination, never directly from a handler.

title: The anchor job anchors each tenant's chain at fixed boundaries under the fenced lease
statement: The anchor job MUST, for each tenant through the per-tenant iterator (ST-SUP-RP04-LC05), publish a periodic anchor with the hash of the chain's row with the highest seq and that seq as the count, read from the audit table and never from the chain-head row, to the sink through the outbox, with the tenant on the outbox row (ST-SUP-RP04-LC01). It MUST run only under the controller lease and MUST fence each anchor transaction with the lease (ST-SUP-RP09-LC03), as ST-SUP-RP10-LC20 states for a worker run. Its period boundaries MUST be fixed clock times, the multiples of the anchor period since the Unix epoch. It MUST store the last anchored boundary of each chain in audit_anchor_boundaries in the anchor's transaction, a holder MUST publish at once a boundary that is due and not anchored, also just after it takes the lease, it MUST count each boundary that it anchors late, and a boundary that is due and not anchored MUST be a health signal until it is anchored.

title: The audit tables are partitioned, tenant-walled and append-only, and one owner function maintains them
statement: The DDL text MUST create the audit table partitioned by month on recorded_at, with no default partition; a trigger that raises on UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE on the table and on each partition; the tables audit_chain_heads, audit_anchor_boundaries and audit_retention_checkpoints; row-level security enabled and forced on each of the four tables, with one policy on the transaction-local tenant setting (ST-STD-TXN-R01); and for the runtime role SELECT and INSERT only on the audit table, SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE only on audit_chain_heads and audit_anchor_boundaries, and SELECT only on audit_retention_checkpoints (ST-STD-TXN-R06). It MUST create the function audit_maintain(), owned by the owner role, SECURITY DEFINER, with a fixed search_path and no arguments, whose retention is the audit-log setting at the time the migration runs, with EXECUTE granted to the runtime role only. Each call MUST set a lock timeout, by default 2 s, and MUST do at most one step in the caller's short transaction: create the first missing partition of the current month and the next three months, or write the retention checkpoints of the oldest partition older than the retention (ST-SUP-RP05-LC11) and drop that partition whole; it MUST return whether a step is left, and MUST NOT delete rows. The controller MUST call it in a loop under the controller lease, each call in its own transaction fenced with the lease (ST-SUP-RP09-LC03), and a missing partition for the next month MUST be a health signal. The owner connector stays for the migration job only (ST-SUP-RP04-LC06).

title: A partition drop leaves a retention checkpoint of each chain
statement: Before it drops a partition, the maintenance function (ST-SUP-RP05-LC10) MUST, in the same transaction and for each tenant whose chain has rows in that partition, set the transaction-local tenant to that tenant, write one row into audit_retention_checkpoints with the seq and the hash of the chain's last row in the partition, and enqueue the same values to the sink as an anchor of the kind retention with the tenant on the outbox row. audit_retention_checkpoints MUST have a trigger that raises on UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE, so a checkpoint cannot be moved after it is written.

title: Record writes a transaction's events as one batch and takes the chain lock last
statement: Record MUST take all the audit events of one transaction in one call, MUST lock the chain head of the transaction's tenant once, as the last lock that the caller takes before it commits, and MUST give the events consecutive seq values in the order given. It MUST set recorded_at of each event after it holds the lock, to the greater of the database clock and the chain's last recorded_at, and MUST ignore a recorded_at that the caller gives, so recorded_at never falls along a chain and a partition drop never cuts a chain in its middle. RecordOutcome and RecordRead MUST each lock the head of their tenant's chain in their own short transaction. Because the command runtime calls Record only after the fill returns (ST-SUP-RP10-LC06), a read row that the fill causes never waits on the chain lock of its own command; one chain per tenant with this late lock is enough, and a read row needs no chain of its own.

title: Untrusted values are cleaned, states pass the redaction, and no value reaches an error
statement: New MUST clean each untrusted value, actor_ip and user_agent, before it is hashed and stored: it MUST replace invalid UTF-8 with U+FFFD, remove NUL and cut the value to at most 512 bytes of valid UTF-8. before, after and patch MUST be settable only through the redacting path of ST-SUP-RP05-LC03, never as raw values. An error that the package returns MUST NOT carry a field value. RecordOutcome and RecordRead MUST always give the event a new ID. A failed RecordOutcome MUST be counted, and returned as an error that names no value, so the command runtime can log its metadata (ST-SUP-RP10-LC06).

title: The decision port has the AuthZEN shape, and deny is a decision
statement: The decision port MUST offer an evaluation of one subject, action, resource, context and consistency that returns a decision with allowed, token and reason; a batch evaluation of several requests with execute_all as the default semantic; and a resource search by subject, action, resource type, context, consistency and page, with an opaque page token. A deny MUST be a decision with allowed false and MUST NOT be an error.

title: The relationships port writes idempotently and returns the written-at token
statement: Relationships MUST expose Touch(tuples, preconditions) and Delete(filters, preconditions), both idempotent on retry and both returning the token the provider wrote at, and the port MUST be reachable only by the relay destination, never by a handler or a slot fill.

title: The floor is at_least(token), and minimize-latency does not exist
statement: Consistency MUST be either fresh or at least as fresh as a token, the runtime MUST NOT expose a minimize-latency or an exact-snapshot option, and an evaluation MUST refuse a zero consistency, so every check runs at least as fresh as the token stored on the resource row.

title: A token is stored per row, and the pages of a list share one floor
statement: The authorization token MUST be an opaque comparable value with a text column form stored on every protected row, and a read of one row MUST check at least as fresh as the row's token. Every later page of a list filtered by batch evaluation MUST run at least as fresh as the fresher of the first page's token and the service's revocation floor at the time of that page (ST-SUP-RP06-LC13), so no later page is checked against an older state than the first page. The pages are not one snapshot, because ST-SUP-RP06-LC03 forbids an exact snapshot: a relation written while the list is paged MAY change what a later page shows.

title: The SpiceDB provider maps the port one to one
statement: The SpiceDB provider MUST speak gRPC, map fresh to fully_consistent and at-least-as-fresh to at_least_as_fresh, write with TOUCH and DELETE only, wrap the after_result_cursor in the opaque page token, and MUST NOT expose at_exact_snapshot.

title: The relay is FIFO per resource key and parks a poison entry
statement: The outbox destination authz MUST be registered as idempotent and as must land, MUST deliver tuples in order per resource key, MUST store the returned token on the owning row, and MUST park an entry that fails with a permanent error, raise an alert and continue with the other keys, so one malformed write never halts the relay and a parked entry leaves only when it is sent again.

title: Every principal is a subject, and a service account is one too
statement: Subject MUST map the Identity to the declared subject type and id, a worker, controller or relay MUST call with its own service_account:<name> subject, and the package MUST expose no bypass flag, setting or subject.

title: Caveat context is a map, and a missing field is an error
statement: Context MUST be a string-keyed map built from the declared context fields, and a CONDITIONAL_PERMISSION result or a missing caveat field MUST be returned as an error, not as a deny, because it means the declaration forgot a context field.

title: The handle decides at the floor and declares relations only through the outbox
statement: The handle MUST be bound to the current transaction and tenant, its evaluation MUST call the decision port with the transaction's principal as subject and, as consistency, at least as fresh as the row token or the service's revocation floor (ST-SUP-RP06-LC13), whichever is fresher, and its relate and unrelate MUST enqueue a touch or delete tuple in the transaction's outbox for the authz destination and MUST NOT call the provider.

title: The handle holds only its allowed relations and no provider
statement: Handle MUST be constructed with the allowed relation set the generated code passes it, MUST refuse any other relation with an error before enqueueing anything, MUST give a system principal its service_account subject, and MUST expose no provider client, no relationships port and no bypass.

title: Every provider passes the conformance suite
statement: The conformance suite MUST run one allow and one deny per permission and the new-enemy test, in which a check at least as fresh as the token of a removed relation denies; search MUST be an optional group, and a provider that does not search MUST report so, after which every list uses batch evaluation.

title: A transaction's tuple writes are one revocation, complete only when the relay lands it
statement: A transaction MUST have one revocation, with its identity known before the commit, which every tuple the transaction enqueues joins, touch or delete, from Relate, Unrelate or a relationship mapper, because a touch can also remove access (view = viewer - banned); Relate and Unrelate MUST return that one revocation; Wait MUST be Status (ST-SUP-RP06-LC15) that waits until the state is no longer pending or its context ends, and MUST be refused before the commit; and a revocation is complete only when the relay lands every tuple of it.

title: After a revocation lands, every check of the service is at least as fresh as its token
statement: The relay MUST keep the service's revocation floor in the table authz_floor, one row of a token and its comparable revision, and MUST raise it to the token of each tuple it delivers, touch or delete, in its own short transaction before the delivery is done, with one update that only raises the revision, so concurrent relays never lower it and never wait for more than that one statement; and every single evaluation, batch evaluation and resource search, and every page of a list, MUST run at least as fresh as the floor and, for one row, as its row token, so a write that removes access through a group, an exclusion or a subject in two tenants is in force on every resource of every tenant, and every check runs at least at the token of the newest delivered tuple write.

title: A revocation that is not delivered in time raises an alert
statement: The relay MUST raise one alert event and metric that name the destination authz on each upward crossing of outbox.oldest.age{destination=authz} (ST-SUP-RP01-LC07) past the delivery alert bound, and none while the gauge stays above the bound.

title: A revocation status is read only by the tenant and principal that made the write
statement: Status MUST read a revocation by its identity only for the tenant and principal that made the write and MUST answer not found to any other pair; and it MUST report failed when a person discarded any tuple of the revocation, otherwise parked while any tuple is parked, otherwise pending until every tuple is done, and complete with the freshest of their tokens when all are done.

title: The delivery alert bound defaults to 5 seconds and is positive
statement: The delivery alert bound MUST default to 5 seconds when no bound is given, and the relay MUST refuse a bound that is not positive.

title: The key table is scoped by tenant, principal and key
statement: The migration text MUST create idempotency_keys with tenant_id, principal_id, key (at most 255 characters), fingerprint, status (in_progress or completed), response_code, response_headers, response_body, locked_at and expires_at, with the primary key (tenant_id, principal_id, key), so one client's key never collides with another's.

title: The key row is inserted first and completed in the same transaction
statement: Wrap MUST insert the key row with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING inside the store's write transaction before the handler runs, and MUST write status completed, the response code, headers and body and expires_at in that same transaction, so a crash leaves no key without its row and no row without its key.

title: A duplicate in progress gets 409, a changed body 422, and a match a replay
statement: When the insert returns nothing, Wrap MUST SELECT FOR UPDATE NOWAIT the row and answer 409 idempotency-key-in-progress when the lock fails or status is in_progress, 422 idempotency-key-reused when the fingerprints differ, and otherwise replay the stored code, headers and body byte for byte with Idempotent-Replayed: true without running the handler.

title: A transient failure stores nothing
statement: A response with status 5xx, 429 or 503, and a 409 with the code conflict (ST-SUP-RC32-OC10), MUST NOT be stored and its key row MUST go with the rollback, and an operation declared as requiring the key MUST answer 400 when the Idempotency-Key header is absent or is not a structured string.

title: The fingerprint is SHA-256 over method, path and canonical body
statement: Fingerprint MUST be the lower-case hexadecimal SHA-256 over the method, the path and the canonical JSON body, each part prefixed by its length in bytes as a 4-byte big-endian unsigned integer, where canonical JSON has sorted object keys, no insignificant whitespace and one form for numbers, so the same request gives the same fingerprint on every replica.

title: An outgoing key derives from the inbound key with its scope, the destination and the effect
statement: Derive MUST return the lower-case hexadecimal SHA-256 over the tenant ID, the principal ID, the inbound key, the destination name and the effect name, which the declaration gives each outgoing call, each part prefixed by its length in bytes as a 4-byte big-endian unsigned integer. Derive MUST return the same value on every retry of the same inbound request, so a fan-out from one inbound request is idempotent at every destination. Two tenants or two principals that send the same inbound key MUST NOT get one outgoing key, and two effects of one request at one destination MUST NOT get one outgoing key, because the inbound key is unique only in the scope of ST-SUP-RP07-LC01.

title: Purge is a bounded batched delete at 24 hours
statement: Purge MUST delete rows whose expires_at has passed in batches of a bounded size with a pause between batches, MUST NOT delete row by row or rely on a TTL index, and the default retention MUST be 24 hours.

title: The conformance tests cover replay, reuse, race and crash
statement: The conformance suite MUST prove a replay of the same body, 422 for a different body, 409 for a concurrent duplicate, and that a crash before commit leaves no key row, and every store that binds the wrapper MUST pass it.

title: Money is int64 minor units with a currency, and adds only within one currency
statement: Money MUST hold an int64 amount of minor units and an ISO 4217 code, Add and Sub MUST return an error when the currencies differ, MUST return an error on overflow, and the package MUST expose no float conversion.

title: Allocation loses no minor unit
statement: Allocate MUST split an amount by the given ratios into parts whose sum equals the amount exactly, assign the remainder one minor unit at a time in a fixed order, and MUST refuse an empty or all-zero ratio set.

title: A transfer is inserted with its entries in one statement that must balance
statement: Post MUST insert the transfer and at least two entries in one statement, MUST reject the set when the debits do not equal the credits or when an entry's currency differs from the ledger's, and MUST take the row lock only on accounts declared with a balance limit.

title: A pending transfer is immutable, and it is posted or voided once
statement: Pend MUST write a pending transfer whose amount and entries no later call edits, posting or voiding a pending transfer MUST write a new row that names it, and the state machine MUST return already_posted, already_voided, expired or exceeds_pending as its only errors, so a change to a pending transfer is a void and a new pend.

title: A retried transfer returns the original
statement: Post and Pend MUST insert with ON CONFLICT (ledger_id, idempotency_key) DO NOTHING RETURNING, and a retry with a key already used MUST return the original transfer and insert no entry.

title: A reversal is a new transfer that names the original, at most once
statement: Reverse MUST insert a new transfer with opposite entries that sets reverses on the new row and reversed_by on the original, MUST refuse a transfer that is already reversed or not posted, and the package MUST expose no difference adjustment.

title: A balance derives from entries after the latest snapshot, on the account's normal side
statement: Balance MUST return the latest snapshot plus the sum of the entries posted after it, signed by the account's normal balance (debit or credit), the balance at a time MUST select by effective_at, and every entry MUST keep both effective_at and posted_at.

title: The snapshot and check jobs run under the lease, and a failed check is a health signal
statement: Snapshot MUST write one balance_snapshots row per account after the declared number of entries, Check MUST verify that every ledger sums to zero, that each snapshot equals its recomputed sum and that expired pending transfers are voided, both MUST run in controller mode under the lease with the fencing token, and a failed check MUST mark the service unhealthy.

title: The guard trigger refuses every update and delete
statement: The DDL text MUST create a BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger that raises on transfers and entries, allow the transfer status to change only through the post and void function and only from pending, and grant the runtime role SELECT and INSERT only.

title: A mode is a named component set, selected by a repeatable flag with all as the default
statement: Parsing the modes MUST accept the mode option more than once and the STEGO_MODE environment value, which holds a comma-separated list of modes, MUST use the mode options alone and ignore STEGO_MODE when any mode option is given, MUST default to all, MUST refuse an unknown mode at startup, and the registry MUST map each mode name to a component set the generated code registers, never to a fixed bundle.

title: A lease is one row, acquired and renewed by one UPDATE that increments the token
statement: Acquire and Renew MUST run UPDATE leases SET holder=$1, expires_at=now()+ttl, token=token+1 WHERE name=$2 AND (holder=$1 OR expires_at<now()) RETURNING token with the defaults lease 15 s, renew 10 s and retry 2 s, and the package MUST NOT use a session-scoped advisory lock.

title: Every write under the lease carries the fencing token and fails on a higher one
statement: A write made through the lease MUST carry the holder's token, MUST fail with the fenced error when the lease row holds a higher token, and the holder's loop MUST stop on the fenced error.

title: A holder that cannot renew stops before the lease expires
statement: When Renew fails or returns a different token, the holder MUST stop its work within one renew interval and before expires_at, and MUST NOT act on the lease after that time.

title: Each mode has its own readiness
statement: Ready MUST answer per mode: api ready when the HTTP server accepts requests, worker ready when the database is reachable, controller ready when the database is reachable, whether or not it holds the lease, and no backfill of it is stalled (ST-SUP-RP09-LC12), and a replica MUST report not ready as the first step of shutdown.

title: Each mode shuts down in its own order
statement: On SIGTERM the sequencer MUST, for api, fail readiness, wait the endpoint propagation delay and drain in-flight requests; for worker, stop claiming and finish the claimed rows; for controller, flush the checkpoint under the lease with the holder's token and then release the lease; and the sequencer MUST run the sequences of every selected mode.

title: The checkpoint row carries the fencing token and refuses a lower one
statement: The checkpoint statement MUST update the change's row in stego_schema.backfills only when the row's token is not higher than the holder's, MUST set the row's token to the holder's, and MUST fail with the fenced error when the row holds a higher token, so that the row lock orders two writers and a stale holder cannot move the checkpoint after a newer one.

title: Backfill progress goes through the probe as counts
statement: The backfill MUST report each batch, the rows that fail the conversion, the duplicate groups, completion and a stall only as the built-in schema backfill observations of the probe runtime (ST-SUP-RP12-LC23), with counts and the change ID and no row value.

title: A backfill batch is one short transaction
statement: Each backfill batch that the generated controller runs MUST be one transaction with a lock timeout, by default 2 s, over at most the batch size, by default 1,000 rows, after the checkpoint key in key order, and MUST write the checkpoint in that transaction.

title: The backfill resumes from its checkpoint and marks completion
statement: After a restart or a takeover the backfill MUST start after the checkpoint key, and when a batch finds no row left it MUST mark the change complete with its time.

title: A new fill value starts a repair pass
statement: When the declared fill value of a retype differs from the fill digest in its checkpoint row, the backfill MUST clear the completed time and the checkpoint key, record the new digest, and pass again over the rows whose new value is unset.

title: A stalled backfill fails readiness, never liveness
statement: A backfill with rows left that commits no batch for three lease TTLs MUST make the readiness of the controller mode (ST-SUP-RP09-LC05) not ready and emit schema.backfill.stalled, MUST NOT fail liveness or stop the process, and MUST make readiness ready again when its next batch commits.

title: The handle is bound to one transaction, tenant and principal
statement: Handle MUST be constructed only with the open store transaction, the tenant and the principal that the generated code passes it, and MUST expose the tenant and the principal for reading only, with no way to change any of the three.

title: No raw database connection is reachable through the handle
statement: The handle MUST NOT expose a *sql.DB, *sql.Tx, *sql.Conn, a driver connection or a method that takes SQL text, and MUST reach storage only through the generated, tenant-scoped repository operations of the entities the command declares it writes.

title: Every read and write runs in the bound transaction with the tenant set
statement: Each repository operation the handle offers MUST run in the bound transaction, with the transaction-local tenant set and the tenant predicate added, so a fill cannot read or write a row of another tenant.

title: The handle decides through the authorization handle at the floor
statement: The handle's authorization part MUST be the authorization runtime's handle bound to the same transaction, tenant and principal, so each decision a fill asks for runs with the principal as subject at the consistency floor that ST-SUP-RP06-LC09 states, and MUST offer no other decision path and no bypass.

title: The command's permission covers its declared writes
statement: The command's declared permission, decided before the fill (ST-SUP-RC32-OC06), MUST authorize every write the handle makes to the entities the command declares it writes, and the handle MUST NOT make a decision of its own per write, so the declared entities (ST-DECL-INV38) and not a second check limit what the fill can write.

title: Each write through the handle is audited in the transaction
statement: Each write the handle makes MUST write its audit row through the audit runtime in the bound transaction, with the command name as the action, the principal as the actor and the diff redacted by field sensitivity, so a write and its audit row commit or roll back together.

title: Effects leave only through the outbox
statement: The handle's effect staging MUST enqueue each declared effect in the bound transaction's outbox for its declared destination, MUST refuse the destinations authz and audit, so a relationship tuple goes only through the authorization handle (ST-SUP-RP06-LC09, ST-SUP-RP06-LC10) and an audit row only through the audit runtime, MUST NOT deliver anything before the commit, and MUST expose no broker client, provider client or network client.

title: A staged effect carries a key scoped to its tenant, principal, destination, effect and entity
statement: Each effect that the handle stages in Run or RunConsumer MUST name the loaded entity value that it is for (ST-SUP-RP10-LC15), and MUST carry the outgoing idempotency key that Derive gives (ST-SUP-RP07-LC06) over the tenant, the principal, an inbound key, the destination and the effect name, where the inbound key is the command's inbound key, or in RunConsumer the message identity (ST-SUP-RP10-LC19), and then the entity's ID, each prefixed by its length in bytes as a 4-byte big-endian unsigned integer, as ST-SUP-RP10-LC21 states for a tick; the message stores that key at enqueue, as ST-SUP-RP01-LC10 states. The handle MUST refuse a second effect of one name for one entity in one call, so a redelivery is idempotent at the destination and two effects of one call never share a key.

title: Only the generated code ends the transaction
statement: The handle MUST NOT expose commit, rollback, savepoint or a way to begin a transaction, and Run MUST end the transaction after the fill returns.

title: The handle is invalid once the fill returns
statement: As soon as the fill returns or panics, before Run commits or rolls back, every method of the handle and of its authorization, audit and effect parts MUST return an error and do nothing, so a fill that keeps the handle, or a goroutine it started, cannot use the transaction.

title: Run calls the fill inside the idempotency wrapper
statement: Run MUST call the fill inside the idempotency runtime's wrapper with the same transaction that the handle binds, so the key row commits or rolls back with the fill's writes and a replay of a completed key returns the stored result without calling the fill.

title: A panic in the fill rolls back everything
statement: When the fill panics, Run MUST roll back the transaction with every write, audit row, outbox row and key row of it, MUST make the handle invalid, and MUST return an error that does not carry the panic value.

title: A read through the command handle is authorized and audited as a query read
statement: Each read the command handle makes MUST be authorized as ST-SUP-RP11-LC06 and ST-SUP-RP11-LC07 state for the query handle, and each read of a resource of an entity with a pii field MUST be audited as ST-SUP-RP11-LC08 states, so a command reads nothing that a query of the same principal could not read and leaves the same audit trail.

title: The handle gives the fill its command's or worker's probe
statement: Handle MUST give the fill, through Probe, the typed probe that the generated code built for its command or worker and bound to the handle's span context, tenant, principal and command or worker name (ST-SUP-RC34-OC03), and MUST offer no other probe, writer or logger; as ST-SUP-RP10-LC10 states for the rest of the handle, that probe MUST emit nothing once the fill returns or panics (ST-SUP-RP12-LC02).

title: Each entity value through the command handle is a loaded value
statement: Each read and write operation of the handle MUST return the entity as its generated loaded type, such as LoadedReservation, which carries the stored field values and has no exported constructor, no exported field and no conversion from another type, so a fill can get a loaded value only from the handle and cannot build one itself.

title: A worker handle is bound to its service account and, for a message, to the staging principal
statement: RunWorker and RunConsumer MUST bind the handle to the open store transaction, the tenant of the tick or of the claimed outbox row, and the principal service_account:<worker name> (ST-SUP-RP06-LC07). The effect staging of ST-SUP-RP10-LC07 MUST store with each message for a destination that a worker consumes the staging principal and the name of the staging command or worker, and RunConsumer MUST bind them, for reading only, from the claimed row. None of these MUST come from the fill or from the message payload, and each write's audit row MUST name the worker as the action, the service account as the actor and, in RunConsumer, the staging principal as the principal on whose behalf it acted.

title: A worker handle decides on each resource it touches, and a consumer decides as both principals
statement: Because no request resource is decided before a worker fill, the worker handle MUST decide the worker's declared permission on each resource it reads, as ST-SUP-RP11-LC06 and ST-SUP-RP11-LC07 state for a query, and on each resource it writes, or for a create on the parent resource that the call names, at the floor of ST-SUP-RP06-LC09 before the write, with the service account as subject. In RunConsumer it MUST make each such decision a second time with the staging principal as subject and the staging command's or staging worker's own declared permission, which the row's stager names, and MUST allow the read or the write only when both are allowed, so the staging principal is decided on each resource that the payload names and on each other resource that the fill touches, and no principal can make a worker touch a resource that it could not touch through its own command. A deny MUST return the refused error and write nothing, and ST-SUP-RP10-LC05 MUST NOT apply to a worker handle.

title: RunWorker runs one tick of one tenant in one transaction
statement: RunWorker MUST call the fill at most once in one transaction for one tenant and one tick, with no idempotency wrapper, MUST commit only when the fill returns no error, and MUST roll back every write, audit row and staged effect of the transaction otherwise, as ST-SUP-RP10-LC09, ST-SUP-RP10-LC10 and ST-SUP-RP10-LC12 state for Run; each effect that it stages takes the key that ST-SUP-RP10-LC21 gives, not a key of the message identity.

title: RunConsumer calls a worker fill once for each message
statement: RunConsumer MUST insert the consumed message's identity as a key of the idempotency runtime (ST-SUP-RP07-LC01, ST-SUP-RP07-LC02) for the message's tenant and the worker's principal in the bound transaction before it calls the fill, MUST return success without calling the fill when that key is already completed, and MUST use that identity as the inbound key from which ST-SUP-RP10-LC08 derives each staged effect's key, so a message that the outbox delivers again after the commit (ST-SUP-RC18-OC27) changes nothing a second time and stages the same keys.

title: A fenced worker run writes nothing
statement: When the generated code passes RunWorker a held lease, RunWorker MUST lock the lease row with FOR SHARE in the bound transaction right after the tenant setting and before the fill, MUST roll back with the fenced error and not call the fill when the row holds a token other than the holder's, and MUST keep the lock until the transaction ends, so a new holder cannot take the lease (ST-SUP-RP09-LC02) while the run can still commit, and every write of the run carries the holder's token (ST-SUP-RP09-LC03).

title: A tick's effect has one key on every replica
statement: Each effect that a worker fill stages in RunWorker MUST name the loaded entity value that it is for, and its outgoing key MUST be the one that Derive gives (ST-SUP-RP07-LC06) over the tenant, the worker's service account, an inbound key, the destination and the effect name, where the inbound key is the worker name, the scheduled tick time and the entity's ID, each prefixed by its length in bytes as a 4-byte big-endian unsigned integer, and the scheduled tick time is the multiple of the interval since the Unix epoch at which the tick is due, as the decimal count of seconds; so every replica that runs the same tick for the same entity stages the same key. The handle MUST refuse a second effect of one name for one entity in one run.

title: A run under a lease ends before the lease can expire
statement: When RunWorker runs under a held lease, it MUST give each tenant's transaction a deadline no later than the lease TTL minus the renew interval after the transaction starts and no later than the lease's expires_at as last renewed, MUST roll back a transaction that reaches the deadline, and MUST NOT commit after expires_at, so the holder stops in time as ST-SUP-RP09-LC04 states; the tenant of a transaction that is rolled back for this reason MUST be run again in the next tick.

title: A locked read holds its row until the transaction ends
statement: Handle MUST offer, for each entity that the command or the worker declares it writes, GetForUpdate and GetForDelete. GetForUpdate MUST lock the row with SELECT ... FOR NO KEY UPDATE, so a concurrent insert of a child row, whose foreign key check takes FOR KEY SHARE on it, does not wait for the lock; GetForDelete MUST lock it with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, for a fill that will delete the row or change a column of its primary key, of a unique index or of a key that a foreign key references, so the write does not make the lock stronger later. Each MUST run in the bound transaction, after the tenant setting and with the tenant predicate (ST-SUP-RP10-LC03), MUST first read the row without a lock and decide the read on it, as ST-SUP-RP10-LC13 states for a command handle and as ST-SUP-RP10-LC17 states for a worker handle, which decides as both principals in RunConsumer, MUST NOT lock a row that is denied and MUST return it as not found with no data from it, and MUST decide again when the row's authorization token changed between the read and the lock (ST-SUP-RP06-LC04). The lock MUST stay until Run, RunWorker or RunConsumer ends the transaction, and the handle MUST offer no way to release it earlier. For a rule over a set of rows, such as the last active admin of an organization, the fill of every command, worker or consumer that can break the rule, also one that inserts a row into the set or removes one from it, MUST lock the parent row with GetForUpdate before it writes, and MUST read the set with a statement that starts after it holds that lock, because a row lock does not stop the insert of a new row into the set.

title: A write through the handle carries the version of its loaded value
statement: Each update and delete through the handle MUST take the loaded value that a read or an earlier write of the same transaction returned, MUST write only when the row's resource version is the version that the loaded value carries (ST-SUP-RC01-OC07), and otherwise MUST write nothing, write no audit row and return the conflict error. A write MUST return a loaded value with the new version, so a second write of the same row in the same transaction does not conflict with the first. An update that changes a column of the row's primary key, of a unique index or of a key that a foreign key references MUST take a loaded value that GetForDelete locked, and MUST refuse with an internal error and write nothing when the value was not locked or was locked by GetForUpdate. A write MUST refuse with an internal error, not the conflict error, a loaded value that another transaction returned, such as one that a fill kept from an earlier attempt, and a loaded value of the same transaction whose row a later write through the handle has changed, because a rerun cannot change the result.

title: A conflict runs the fill again only as the command declares
statement: Run MUST treat as a conflict the conflict error of ST-SUP-RP10-LC24 and a database error with the SQLSTATE 40001, 40P01 or 55P03 from any statement of the attempt that the fill or the generated code runs, the outbox enqueue and COMMIT included. The statements of the idempotency wrapper are not in this class: a lock that Wrap cannot take with NOWAIT, a lock timeout while its key insert waits on a duplicate key, or a cancel at the deadline during a statement of the wrapper MUST stay the answer 409 idempotency-key-in-progress of ST-SUP-RP07-LC03, with no rerun, and any other database error from a statement of the wrapper, the SQLSTATE 40001 and 40P01 included, MUST be an internal error, with no rerun. Once the handle meets a conflict, every later method of the handle MUST return the conflict error and do nothing, and Run MUST treat the call as a conflict whatever the fill returns, so a fill cannot ignore a conflict and commit. On a conflict Run MUST roll back the whole transaction as ST-SUP-RC32-OC05 states and, while fewer reruns than the command's Retry on conflict (ST-DECL-EN18) have run and the deadline allows a rerun (ST-SUP-RP10-LC28), MUST call the fill again after a random wait of at most 50 ms times the number of the rerun, capped and checked as ST-SUP-RP10-LC28 states, in a new transaction that the generated code opens with the tenant set as ST-SUP-RC32-OC04 states, with a new handle, the same idempotency key (ST-SUP-RP10-LC11) and a new decode of the request body, so a fill that changed its request does not see its change again. Run MUST NOT call the fill again when the outcome of COMMIT is not known, such as when the connection is lost during it or the deadline cancels it (ST-SUP-RP10-LC28), and MUST then return an internal error, for which the handler writes an audit row with the outcome failed and the fixed error_code commit_outcome_unknown in its own short transaction (ST-SUP-RC32-OC07); when that commit took effect, its own audit row with the outcome ok stays as well, so a retry of the client with the same key replays the stored result or runs the command once. After the last attempt Run MUST return the conflict to the handler. Each attempt is one call for the probe (ST-SUP-RP12-LC20): its emissions are held, counted against the limit and sent as their observation counts for that attempt alone.

title: A conflict in a worker run rolls back and waits for the next run
statement: RunWorker and RunConsumer MUST treat a conflict as ST-SUP-RP10-LC25 states and MUST NOT run the fill again in the same transaction or the same tick. RunWorker MUST roll back that tenant's transaction and MUST run that tenant again in the next tick, as ST-SUP-RP10-LC22 states for a deadline. RunConsumer MUST roll back the message's transaction with its key row (ST-SUP-RP10-LC19) and return an error marked as a conflict, not as a failure, so the message is not completed and the relay dispatches it again as ST-SUP-RP01-LC18 and ST-SUP-RC18-OC29 state, with the same outgoing keys.

title: A locked list is bounded and locks only allowed rows in key order
statement: Handle MUST offer ListForUpdate only for an entity that declares it writes and that declares Lock at most (ST-DECL-EN02, ST-DECL-INV81). ListForUpdate MUST first read the matching rows without a lock, with a limit of Lock at most plus one, and when more rows than Lock at most match MUST lock nothing, return no row and return an internal error, never the conflict error and never a shorter list. It MUST then filter the rows by the decision port as ST-SUP-RP10-LC13 states for a command handle and as ST-SUP-RP10-LC17 states for a worker handle, MUST lock only the allowed rows, with SELECT ... WHERE the primary key is one of them, the list's filter applied again and ORDER BY the primary key FOR NO KEY UPDATE, so two fills that lock the same rows lock them in one order, MUST decide again each locked row whose authorization token changed after the first read (ST-SUP-RP06-LC04) and leave out a row that is now denied, and MUST return the locked, allowed rows in primary key order. The locks MUST stay as ST-SUP-RP10-LC23 states.

title: A lock wait ends before the request deadline as a conflict
statement: Before each statement of an attempt that can wait for a row lock, which includes each read with a lock and each write through the handle, the statements of the generated code after the fill and COMMIT, Run, RunWorker and RunConsumer MUST set SET LOCAL lock_timeout in the bound transaction to the smaller of the command's declared Lock timeout (ST-DECL-EN18), or 2 s for a command that declares none and for a worker, and the time left before the deadline of the request or the run less 50 ms, and to at least 1 ms, so a statement that waits for a row lock ends with the SQLSTATE 55P03, which is a conflict (ST-SUP-RP10-LC25), and no lock wait holds a pooled connection without a limit. The first setting MUST come right after the tenant setting and before the idempotency key insert (ST-SUP-RP07-LC02). A cancel at the deadline, or another context error, during a statement before COMMIT MUST also count as a conflict, also when the driver closes the connection on the cancel, as pgx does. During COMMIT, a cancel or another context error MUST count as an outcome of COMMIT that is not known (ST-SUP-RP10-LC25) and never as a conflict, because the commit can have taken effect. Run MUST cap the random wait before a rerun (ST-SUP-RP10-LC25) so that at least 100 ms is left before the deadline after the wait, MUST check the time left after the wait, and MUST NOT start a rerun when less than 100 ms is left then; it MUST then return the conflict of the attempt before it.

title: Read audit rows have connections of their own
statement: The generated store MUST keep a pool of at least two connections apart from the main pool, which only the short audit transactions of ST-SUP-RP05-LC02 use, so the read audit row of a fill that holds row locks and a main connection never waits for a main connection, and MUST give each such transaction a lock timeout and a statement timeout of at most 2 s, so an audit write that cannot finish fails the read as ST-SUP-RP11-LC08 states and does not wait without a limit.

title: The query handle is bound to one read-only transaction, tenant and principal
statement: Handle MUST be constructed only with the open read-only store transaction, the tenant and the principal that the generated code passes it, and MUST expose the tenant and the principal for reading only, with no way to change any of the three.

title: No raw database connection is reachable through the query handle
statement: The handle MUST NOT expose a *sql.DB, *sql.Tx, *sql.Conn, a driver connection or a method that takes SQL text, and MUST reach storage only through the generated, tenant-scoped repository reads of the entities the query declares it reads.

title: Every read runs in the bound transaction with the tenant set
statement: Each repository read the handle offers MUST run in the bound transaction, with the transaction-local tenant set and the tenant predicate added, so a fill cannot read a row of another tenant.

title: The query handle can write nothing
statement: The handle MUST offer no create, update, delete, relate, unrelate or effect staging, and the bound transaction MUST be READ ONLY, so a write that reaches the database through any path still fails there.

title: The query handle decides through the authorization handle at the floor
statement: The handle's authorization part MUST be the authorization runtime's handle bound to the same transaction, tenant and principal, so each decision runs with the principal as subject at the consistency floor that ST-SUP-RP06-LC09 states, and MUST offer no other decision path, no bypass and no relate or unrelate.

title: A read of a protected resource needs an allow
statement: Each read the handle makes of an entity with a resource type MUST first evaluate the permission that the entity declares for read through the authorization handle, and MUST return a deny as not found with no data from the row.

title: A list through the query handle holds only allowed rows
statement: A list the handle returns for an entity with a resource type MUST be filtered by the decision port, on the query's declared permission for a list query and on the permission the entity declares for list otherwise, in the way the entity's expected cardinality declares, and every page MUST be checked at the one at_least floor that ST-SUP-RP06-LC04 and ST-SUP-RP06-LC09 give a list.

title: A read of personal data is audited per resource with the action read
statement: When the fill reads a resource of an entity with a pii field, Run MUST record one audit row for each such resource with the action read, the principal as the actor and the query name as an annotation, each in its own short transaction as ST-SUP-RP05-LC02 states, through the audit connections of ST-SUP-RP10-LC29, before the result returns, and MUST return no result when a write fails.

title: The query handle is invalid once the fill returns
statement: As soon as the fill returns or panics, before Run ends the transaction, every method of the handle and of its authorization part MUST return an error and read nothing, so a fill that keeps the handle, or a goroutine it started, cannot read outside its query.

title: A failed or panicking fill returns no result
statement: When the fill returns an error or panics, Run MUST end the transaction, make the handle invalid and return no result, with an error that does not carry the panic value.

title: The handle gives the fill its query's probe
statement: Handle MUST give the fill, through Probe, the typed probe that the generated code built for its query and bound to the handle's span context, tenant, principal and query name (ST-SUP-RC34-OC03), and MUST offer no other probe, writer or logger; as ST-SUP-RP11-LC09 states for the rest of the handle, that probe MUST emit nothing once the fill returns or panics (ST-SUP-RP12-LC02).

title: Each entity value through the query handle is a loaded value
statement: Each read operation of the handle MUST return the entity as its generated loaded type, such as LoadedReservation, which carries the stored field values and has no exported constructor, no exported field and no conversion from another type, so a fill can get a loaded value only from the handle and cannot build one itself.

title: A streamed query sends only allowed loaded values, each decided at the floor
statement: For a query served as a server stream, the handle MUST offer Send, which MUST take only a loaded entity value (ST-SUP-RP11-LC12), MUST decide the read permission that the entity declares for it with the principal as subject at the floor of ST-SUP-RP06-LC09 at the time of the send, MUST send the message only on an allow and drop and count it on a deny, MUST read through the bound read-only transaction alone, and MUST return an error and send nothing once the stream ends or the fill returns.

title: A probe takes no free-text message
statement: The runtime's emit function MUST take only a generated observation descriptor and typed values that match the descriptor's fields in order, and MUST offer no message, format string, free attribute, error value or other parameter that the declaration does not declare; an emission with a value of the wrong kind or count, or with a measure outside its declared range, MUST be dropped and counted, never sent.

title: A probe is bound to its call and goes quiet once the fill returns
statement: A probe MUST be constructed only with the span context, the tenant, the principal and the name of the command, query, worker or slot binding that the generated code passes it, and MUST expose no way to change any of them; as soon as the fill returns or panics, as ST-SUP-RP10-LC10 and ST-SUP-RP11-LC09 state for the handle, each method of the probe MUST emit nothing and count the attempt, so a fill that keeps the probe, or a goroutine it started, cannot emit outside its call.

title: A log record carries opaque correlation only
statement: Each log record and console line MUST carry the name, the trace ID and span ID of the bound span context when it is valid, the tenant ID, the principal's opaque ID and the operation name, which the runtime adds and the fill cannot set, and MUST NOT carry a name, an email address or a claim of the principal; who did what stays in the audit trail (ST-SUP-RP05).

title: An event becomes a log record and a span event
statement: When the telemetry runtime (ST-SUP-RP03) has a log provider, each emission of an event MUST become one log record named domain.<name> with the declared severity, the declared fields as attributes and no body text, and, when the bound span is recording, one event of the same name on that span with only the attributes that ST-SUP-RP12-LC13 allows.

title: A counter or histogram becomes a metric
statement: When the telemetry runtime has a meter provider, each counter MUST be one monotonic integer counter named domain.<name> that adds one for each emission, and each histogram one floating-point histogram named domain.<name> in its declared unit that records the emitted value, each with only the attributes that ST-SUP-RP12-LC13 allows.

title: OTLP is on when a collector endpoint is set
statement: The runtime MUST send OTLP signals through the telemetry runtime when, and only when, the telemetry runtime has a collector endpoint at start.

title: The console sink writes one line per emission to standard output
statement: When ST-SUP-RP12-LC16 turns it on for declared observations, the console sink MUST write one line for each of their emissions of every kind to the process's standard output, as one JSON object or one logfmt line, with the timestamp, the severity, the service name, the instance identity, the name, the declared fields, the histogram value, the stego.outcome of an observation that counts each attempt, and the correlation of ST-SUP-RP12-LC03.

title: Emitting never blocks, fails or panics the fill
statement: An emission MUST return with no result and MUST NOT wait on a sink: each sink MUST take records through its own bounded queue of at most 1,024 records that drops rather than blocks, and a failing or blocked sink MUST NOT change, delay or stop the call.

title: A probe carries no private value
